sentences.text:
This is an application filed under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code praying for quashing of First Information Report in Crime No.1034/2022 and the consequent Final Report/Charge-sheet No.128/2023 dated 17.3.2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 420,
468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 5 of the Maharashtra Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887.

As per the contents of the said First Information Report the respondent No.2 on receiving secret information conducted raid on the house of one Sachin Yerone residing at Saturna area wherein it was found that said Sachin was indulged in the activity of cricket betting, as the match between India and New Zealand was going on.
It was found that said Sachin with the aid of cellphones was doing betting.
Two cellphones and chargers were found from his person and an offence came to be registered against him and applicant under Sections mentioned above.
After completion of investigation the prosecution filed a charge-sheet in the matter.
The present application was accordingly amended and the charge-sheet so filed is also challenged.
3. We have heard Mr. J.B. Kasat, learned counsel for the applicant and Mr. N.B. Jawade, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the First Information is completely silent about the nature of forgery of valuable security so also using as genuine a forged document or electronic record by the applicant and, therefore, no offence alleged under Sections 420, 468 and 471 are made out against him.
He further states that admittedly respondent No.2/first informant is not a person who is cheated nor there is any allegation of forgery of valuable security.

It is his further submission that there is nothing on record to suggest that the applicant has committed an offence as punishable under Sections 4 and 5 of the Gambling Act and even reading of the provisions of the Act in conjunctions with the contents of the F.I.R. and the material along with charge-sheet, no offence is made out under the said Section.
In nutshell, it is the submission of the counsel for the applicant that the First Information Report is nothing but an abuse of process of the Court and, therefore, is liable to be quashed.
5. On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor strongly opposed the contentions advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant.
He submits that during the investigation it is revealed that co-accused Sachin was in constant contact with the present applicant on cellphone.
He further submits that both accused persons have created fake ID with passport on the website and were indulged in the offence of betting.
6. We have carefully perused the material on record along with legal provisions.

To bring home an offence under Sections 420, 468 and 471, it is imperative on the prosecution to show that there is cheating as well as any nature of forgery of valuable security or using as genuine a forged document or electronic record by the applicant.
As can be seen from the First Information Report nothing of such nature has been stated nor there is any supporting material to show that there is any forgery of any valuable security or otherwise.
The only allegation against the present applicant is that the accused namely Sachin Yerone for his financial gains was in contact with the present applicant.

Furthermore, even though there are WhatsApp chats of which screen shots are produced along with the charge-sheet, there is nothing incriminating to implicate the present applicant and to show that it was he who was indulged in the offence as stated in the F.I.R.

sentences.text: As far as offences under Sections 4 and 5 of the Gambling Act are concerned what is imperative is that the person should keep or use any house, room or case for the purpose of common gaming house or being the owner/occupier of any such house willfully permits the same to be used for any other purpose.
Furthermore, Section 5 of the said Act contemplates presence of person in common gaming house.
Nothing of this sort has been pleaded in the F.I.R. and the consequent charge-sheet.
Except for call records there is nothing incriminating as far as present applicant is concerned.

There is nothing in the charge-sheet which connects the present applicant with the offences alleged of in the F.I.R.
8.

It would, be therefore, a case to exercise inherent jurisdiction as the situation is squarely covered by the parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal and others, reported in AIR 1992 SC 604 the allegations made in the First Information Report even if they are taken on their face value and accepted in their entirety do not make out a case against the accused.

sentences.text: 9. We, therefore, quash and set aside the First Information Report bearing No.1034/2022 and the consequent Final Report/Charge-sheet No.128/2023 dated 17.3.2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 5 of the Maharashtra Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887.

Accordingly, we proceed to pass following order :
ORDER (i) The application is allowed.

(ii) First Information Report in Crime No.1034/2022 and the consequent Final Report/Charge-sheet No.128/2023 dated 17.3.2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 5 of the Maharashtra Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887 is quash and set aside as far as present applicant is concerned.
(iii) Application is disposed of.
(Nandesh S. Deshpande, J.) (Urmila Joshi-Phalke, J.) wadode
